matchstick.title: Balance by numeric difference and single‑stick transformation
matchstick.principle: Before moving any stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation (including any addition or subtraction). Use the difference to guide which transformation can balance the equation with a single stick move.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever the equation is false and you need to decide which stick to move.
matchstick.example: Computing the side values but then moving a stick arbitrarily, resulting in a still‑unbalanced equation.

matchstick.title: Convert V to X to add 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must increase contains a V and the numeric imbalance is exactly +5, move one of V’s angled sticks to form an X, raising its value by five.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference between sides is +5 and a V is present on the lower‑value side.
matchstick.example: Moving a stick from a V and leaving a single angled stick, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick between numerals
matchstick.principle: Move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral that already has at least one I to another numeral that can accept an extra I, thereby increasing the target by 1 and decreasing the source by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric imbalance is exactly 1 (or a multiple of 1) and both sides contain numerals with I’s.
matchstick.example: Moving an I‑stick from a numeral that then has no I left, producing an invalid numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert X to V to subtract 5
matchstick.principle: If the side that must decrease contains an X and the numeric imbalance is exactly –5, move one of X’s diagonal sticks away (or reposition it) so the X becomes a V, lowering its value by five.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the difference is –5 and an X appears on the higher‑value side.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X and leaving a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral.

matchstick.title: Swap '-' and '=' by moving a horizontal stick
matchstick.principle: If both a minus sign (single horizontal) and an equals sign (two horizontals) are present, you can move one horizontal stick from the equals to the minus, turning the minus into an equals and the equals into a minus.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains both '-' and '=', and the numeric imbalance can be fixed by swapping a horizontal stick.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal from '=' to '-', but forgetting to keep at least one horizontal on '=', turning it into a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '-' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Remove the vertical stick from a plus sign; the remaining horizontal makes it a minus sign, reducing the RHS by 1 (if the plus was part of an addition).
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the RHS is larger by exactly 3 and a '+' appears on that side, moving its vertical stick can reduce the RHS appropriately.
matchstick.example: Removing the vertical from '+' without adjusting the numeric values, leaving the equation false.

matchstick.title: Maintain operator validity when moving a stick from '='
matchstick.principle: When you relocate a stick from the equality sign, ensure that at least one horizontal stick remains so the sign stays a valid '=', otherwise the equation loses its equality operator.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time you consider moving a stick from the '=' sign.
matchstick.example: Taking a horizontal from '=', leaving only one horizontal and thus turning the equality sign into a minus sign.

matchstick.title: Transfer I stick across equality when imbalance is 2
matchstick.principle: If the numeric difference between the two sides is exactly 2, you can move a vertical I‑stick from a numeral on the larger side to a numeral on the smaller side, adjusting both sides by 1 each.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the imbalance is 2 and both sides contain numerals with I’s that can give and receive a stick.
matchstick.example: Moving an I from a numeral that then becomes invalid (e.g., solitary I) and adding it to another numeral that creates a non‑standard numeral.

matchstick.title: Convert '-' to '=' by moving a vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Place a vertical stick onto a minus sign and rotate it to horizontal; the minus gains a second horizontal and becomes an equals sign, while the source numeral loses one I, reducing its value by 1.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '-' and turning subtraction into equality can resolve the numeric imbalance, typically by moving an I‑stick from a numeral on the larger side.
matchstick.example: Moving a vertical stick onto the minus sign but leaving it vertical, creating an invalid operator.

matchstick.title: Convert '+' to '=' by moving its vertical stick
matchstick.principle: Rotate the vertical stick of a plus sign to become a horizontal and place it on the same sign; the plus then has two horizontals and becomes an equals sign, eliminating the addition.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and converting the addition to equality resolves the numeric imbalance, especially when the RHS is too large.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical from '+' without rotating it, leaving a stray vertical and an invalid operator.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from a numeral that cannot lose a stick without becoming invalid (e.g., X, V, solitary I)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model assumes any stick can be removed, ignoring that some numerals need all their sticks to stay valid.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that the source numeral will remain a valid Roman numeral after the stick is removed.

matchstick.description: Providing an invalid equation after moving a stick (including incomplete or unreachable solutions)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on syntactic changes without re‑evaluating the arithmetic truth of the resulting equation.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After each move, recompute the numeric values and verify that the equation holds.

matchstick.description: Moving a stick from the equality sign and leaving no valid ‘=’ sign in the equation
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats the two horizontals of ‘=’ as independent and may move one away, forgetting the sign must stay an equality.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: If you relocate a stick from '=', ensure at least one horizontal remains so the sign stays a valid ‘=’.

matchstick.description: Not verifying numeric equality after transformation; resulting equation may be syntactically valid but numerically false
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model stops after finding a plausible‑looking arrangement and does not double‑check the arithmetic.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Always compute both sides after the move and confirm they are equal.

matchstick.description: Moving more than one stick (or removing multiple sticks) violates the single‑stick rule
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model sometimes chains multiple edits in its reasoning, effectively moving several sticks.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Explicitly count the sticks you relocate; only one stick may be moved.
